short: Germany's most-produced tank, and the only one in service from 1939 to 1945.
full:
Deliveries of the first Ausf. A began in October 1937. The Panzer IV was conceived as a support tank, its short-barrelled 7.5 cm gun firing high-explosive against strongpoints while the Panzer III fought enemy armour. It fought in Poland, France and the opening of the invasion of the Soviet Union in this role, and about 8,500 were built in all.

The encounter with the T-34 and KV-1 reversed the design's purpose. From 1942 the long 7.5 cm KwK 40 turned the Panzer IV into Germany's standard anti-tank weapon, a job it kept to the end of the war because the Panther never fully displaced it. Its chassis carried the Jagdpanzer IV, the Brummbaer and much else. German service ended with the surrender in 1945, but exported and captured examples soldiered on: Syrian Panzer IVs shelled Israeli settlements from the Golan and were still being knocked out in 1967.
